citations.pinpoint: Subd. 4 (income limit for child under 19); Subd. 1a (5% FPG disregard)
citations.quote: To be eligible for medical assistance under section 256B.055, subdivision 3a, a child under age 19 may have income up to 275 percent of the federal poverty guidelines for the household size.
Medical assistance may be paid for a person who is a child under the age of 19
Children 2 through 18: less than or equal to 275% FPG
There is no asset limit for Medical Assistance (MA) for Families with Children and Adults.
The agency must provide Medicaid to children under age 19 whose household income is at or below the income standard established by the agency in its State plan

summary: The spouse is 18, so they fall in Minnesota's Medical Assistance category for children under 19 (Minn. Stat. 256B.055 subd. 3a; 42 CFR 435.118). Its income limit is 275% FPG (256B.056 subd. 4; EPM 2.2.3.3). Neither the statute, the federal rule nor DHS's list of eligibility categories excludes married children, and MA-FCA has no asset test. The engine put the 3-person MAGI household at about 156% FPL ($42,664 against the 2026 guideline of $27,320) and found the spouse eligible under its older-child category. That matches the law, so the reference of 1 holds. The consensus answer of 0 wrongly applied the 133%/138% adult limit.
